careers.parliamentaryService: Elected to the House of Representatives for Oxley, Queensland, at the 1996 general election and defeated at the 1998 election; the Parliament of Australia records her party service in that period as Independent from 2 March 1996 to 27 June 1997 and as Pauline Hanson's One Nation from 27 June 1997 to 3 October 1998. Recorded as Leader of the Federal Parliamentary Pauline Hanson's One Nation from 2 July 2016 and as Leader of One Nation from 28 January 2026, when the party's name changed in the parliamentary record.

integrityMatters.title: Queensland prosecution over the 1997 registration of Pauline Hanson's One Nation: convictions quashed and acquittals entered
integrityMatters.organisation: Supreme Court of Queensland; Queensland Police Service; Queensland Director of Public Prosecutions; District Court of Queensland; Queensland Court of Appeal; Crime and Misconduct Commission (Queensland)
integrityMatters.description: In October 1997 Ms Hanson applied to register Pauline Hanson's One Nation as a Queensland political party on the basis that it had more than 500 members. After a civil challenge, the Supreme Court of Queensland set the registration aside in August 1999, finding the Electoral Commissioner's decision had been induced by fraud or misrepresentation. Following a police investigation, Ms Hanson and David Ettridge were charged in July 2001 with dishonestly inducing the registration, and Ms Hanson was also charged with dishonestly obtaining electoral reimbursements. A District Court jury convicted both on 20 August 2003 and each was sentenced to three years' imprisonment. On 6 November 2003 the Queensland Court of Appeal quashed the convictions, set aside the sentences and directed that verdicts of acquittal be entered. A Crime and Misconduct Commission inquiry requested by the Queensland Parliament found in January 2004 that no misconduct or impropriety was associated with the litigation or the police investigation.

statusHistory.note: A disendorsed candidate instituted Supreme Court proceedings challenging the Queensland registration of the party.
Civil proceedings: the Supreme Court set aside the decision to register the party, finding it had been induced by fraud or misrepresentation; upheld by the Court of Appeal on 10 March 2000.
Matter referred on behalf of the Electoral Commissioner to the Commissioner of Police.

A District Court jury found both guilty; each was sentenced to three years' imprisonment.
The Court of Appeal quashed the convictions, set aside the sentences and directed that verdicts of acquittal be entered.
January 2004: the Crime and Misconduct Commission found no misconduct or impropriety in the litigation or the police investigation, and no evidence of political pressure.

integrityMatters.outcome: Convictions quashed; verdicts of acquittal entered (Queensland Court of Appeal, 6 November 2003). No conviction stands. The Crime and Misconduct Commission (January 2004) found that 'no misconduct or other impropriety has been shown to have been associated with the conduct of the litigation concerning Ms Hanson and Mr Ettridge, or with the police investigations leading to the prosecution'.

integrityMatters.title: Electoral Commission investigation into disclosure of the aircraft used in the party's 2016 campaign (party-level matter)
integrityMatters.description: After an ABC Four Corners program on 3 April 2017 raised questions about the provision of an aircraft used by Pauline Hanson's One Nation during the 2016 campaign, the Australian Electoral Commission examined whether the disclosures required under Part XX of the Commonwealth Electoral Act 1918 had been made. The AEC issued 15 compulsory notices and sought advice from the Commonwealth Director of Public Prosecutions. During the investigation the party amended its 2015–16 return to disclose a $30,500 gift in kind, and other parties lodged donor returns. In its report of 16 November 2018 the AEC concluded that the returns and amended returns lodged provided the relevant disclosure and closed the matter. The report makes no finding about Senator Hanson personally; it is recorded here because she led the party concerned.

statusHistory.note: Four Corners aired allegations about the aircraft; the matter was referred to the AEC.

integrityMatters.outcome: AEC investigation report, 16 November 2018: 'As disclosure in relation to the plane has been achieved, the matter is considered closed.' No finding was made against Senator Hanson.

integrityMatters.title: Electoral Commission review of the party's 2019 election funding claim: overpayment and enforceable undertaking given as party agent
integrityMatters.description: As registered agent for Pauline Hanson's One Nation, Senator Hanson lodged the party's final election funding claim for the 2019 federal election. On review, the AEC found the claim deficient because a number of expenditure items could not be substantiated, being either not electoral expenditure or expenditure that had not been incurred, resulting in an overpayment of $165,442.03. On 4 March 2021 the Electoral Commissioner varied the party's entitlement to $2,675,324.42. Senator Hanson then gave a written undertaking, accepted by the Electoral Commissioner on 15 June 2021 under the Regulatory Powers (Standard Provisions) Act 2014, that future claims would specify all electoral expenditure with invoices matched to evidence of payment. The undertaking was given in her capacity as party agent.

statusHistory.note: The Electoral Commissioner determined the party's entitlement after finding $165,442.03 had been overpaid on unsubstantiated items.
The Electoral Commissioner accepted an enforceable undertaking from Senator Hanson as party agent in respect of the record-keeping provision, section 317(1) of the Commonwealth Electoral Act.

integrityMatters.outcome: Entitlement varied to $2,675,324.42 after an overpayment of $165,442.03 was identified; enforceable undertaking accepted on 15 June 2021. No civil penalty proceedings are recorded.

integrityMatters.title: Federal Court finding that a September 2022 post to Senator Mehreen Faruqi contravened section 18C of the Racial Discrimination Act; appeal dismissed
integrityMatters.organisation: Federal Court of Australia; Full Court of the Federal Court of Australia
integrityMatters.description: After Senator Faruqi posted about the death of Queen Elizabeth II in September 2022, Senator Hanson replied on X telling her to 'piss off back to Pakistan', and Senator Faruqi brought proceedings under the Racial Discrimination Act 1975. On 1 November 2024 Justice Stewart found the post was reasonably likely to offend, insult, humiliate or intimidate on the basis of race, colour or national or ethnic origin, and ordered it deleted within seven days with costs. On 27 July 2026 the Full Court dismissed Senator Hanson's appeal, holding that none of the grounds was established and rejecting her argument that section 18C impermissibly burdens political communication.

statusHistory.note: Justice Stewart found the post unlawful under section 18C and ordered its deletion and costs. Senator Hanson announced an appeal.
The Full Court dismissed the appeal; costs reserved. Senator Hanson said she would consider seeking leave to appeal to the High Court.

integrityMatters.outcome: Appeal dismissed on 27 July 2026; the first-instance orders stand. No High Court application had been located as at 1 October 2026.

integrityMatters.title: Senate censure and seven-sitting-day suspension after wearing a burqa in the chamber
integrityMatters.description: On 24 November 2025, after the Senate declined to allow her to introduce a bill to ban full-face coverings, Senator Hanson entered the chamber wearing a burqa. Proceedings were halted and she was suspended for the rest of the day when she declined to remove it. On 25 November 2025 the Senate agreed to a censure motion moved by the Leader of the Government in the Senate, Senator Penny Wong, and suspended Senator Hanson for seven consecutive sitting days, a penalty that carried into the February 2026 sittings.

integrityMatters.title: High Court ruling that the 2016 election was void under section 44(i) of the Constitution
integrityMatters.organisation: High Court of Australia sitting as the Court of Disputed Returns
integrityMatters.description: On 9 August 2017 the Senate referred questions about Senator Roberts's eligibility to the Court of Disputed Returns after reports that he held British citizenship by descent when he nominated for the 2016 election. On 22 September 2017 Justice Keane found that Senator Roberts was a British citizen at nomination, knew there was at least a real and substantial prospect that he was, and had not taken effective steps to renounce it before nominating; his renunciation took effect on 5 December 2016. On 27 October 2017 the Full Court unanimously held that he had been ineligible to be elected and ordered a special count, under which Fraser Anning was declared elected. In June 2019 the High Court ordered Senator Roberts to pay $6,000 plus costs in an action under the Common Informers (Parliamentary Disqualifications) Act 1975 for the sitting days on which he sat while ineligible. He was elected to the Senate again in 2019.

conductMatters.title: Allegation by former senator Brian Burston of sexual harassment (2019)
conductMatters.allegationSummary: On 14 February 2019 former One Nation senator Brian Burston publicly alleged, in comments reported by The Daily Telegraph and ABC News, that in 1998 Senator Hanson had rubbed her fingers up his spine and that she had propositioned him after his 2016 election. Senator Hanson denied the allegations and described them as retaliation. The allegation was later aired in evidence in defamation proceedings between the two; the court's findings in that case concerned Senator Hanson's statements about Mr Burston, not this allegation. PUBLIC RECORD has located no police report, investigation or finding relating to it.
